title: auth: unify auth header semantics for OpenAI-compat (scoped tokens, nonce, CORS) + signed request support
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed several interoperability issues across the OpenAI-compatibility layer and first-party API surface related to multiple semantics of the Authorization header, project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS preflight behavior, and an attack surface around replayable unsigned streaming requests. This PR unifies header parsing and validation across the server, the OpenAI-compat translation layer, and SDK helpers, introduces an optional signed-request header flow for Private deployments, and standardizes nonce handling for streaming and function/tool-calling flows. Changes are intended to be backwards-compatible by fallbacks and opt-in for signed requests. Summary of changes: 1) server/api/handler: central auth parser that recognizes bearer tokens, project:key patterns, and scoped-tokens with the new "X-Redwood-Nonce" validation; 2) compat/openai layer: align OpenAI-compat Authorization semantics so that requests using "Authorization: Bearer <token>" and project-scoped headers behave the same; support legacy OpenAI-style "OpenAI-Organization" header mapping to internal org routing; 3) signed requests: new optional request-signature header scheme ("X-Redwood-Sig" plus "X-Redwood-Nonce") for Private installs that can be enforced by config; includes verification helpers and a small shim script for key rotation; 4) streaming stability: streaming request path now enforces nonce and signature checks earlier to avoid partially-accepted streams; KV-cache and streaming continuation were updated to keep streaming session IDs tied to validated auth tokens, preventing mixups under heavy load; 5) function/tool calling and structured output: tooling to ensure tool-calling webhook callbacks include the original request signature metadata when routed to customer-managed endpoints; 6) SDK updates: small helper functions in Python/TS SDKs for scoped-token parsing and optional request signing; 7) docs and migration notes: new docs page with examples and a migration checklist for customers to enable signed-requests. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for hosted customers; signed-request verification is off by default and can be enabled via config for Dedicated/Private. Migration notes included in docs. Testing: unit + integration tests added for header permutations, streaming session nonces, and signed-request validation. CI: flaky streaming test re-run addressed; overall CI green. Rollout: feature-flag gated, staged rollout to Dedicated clusters first, then global enable for Private with admin config.
commits_summary: 7 commits: centralize auth parser; add signed-request verifier; compat layer mapping for org/project keys; enforce nonce in streaming path; SDK helpers and docs; tests and CI fixes; add migration docs.
ci_checks_summary: All CI checks passed after one rerun of streaming-integration which was flaky on first run. Lint, unit, integration, and e2e compat tests green. Performance canary executed in staging and met latency SLOs for 95th percentile streaming latency.
review_comments: Miguel Ortiz: Can we ensure legacy OpenAI org headers map to the same internal org id used by project-key routing? Suggest adding explicit tests for both header variants.
Asha Patel (author): Added mapping and unit tests for OpenAI-Organization and X-Redwood-Project headers. See tests/integration/test_streaming_auth.py
Lina Huang: I asked for explicit details on nonce expiry and replay protections. Are nonces single-use or time-windowed? Also check behavior for long-lived streams.

Asha Patel (author): Nonces are single-use for streaming session handshake; short-lived time window (configurable, default 60s) applied for signed-requests. Added comments and config knobs in server/config.go. Updated docs with recommendations for long-running sessions.
Benji Walker: Are there any performance regressions with validating signatures on every request? We should make signature verification optional and cache verified tokens where appropriate.

Asha Patel (author): Signature verification is opt-in and short-circuit cached for token-to-identity mapping for 5 minutes by default. Signature verification happens at session setup for streaming to avoid per-chunk crypto ops. Added cache and bench results to PR description.
Miguel Ortiz: Approving pending small nits in docs and a changelog entry.
release_notes: Unify Authorization header semantics across Redwood and the OpenAI-compat layer. Introduce optional signed-request headers (X-Redwood-Sig, X-Redwood-Nonce) for Private deployments. Standardize nonce handling for streaming and function/tool-calling flows. Migration guide available in docs/openai-compat/auth.md.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flag gated rollout. For Dedicated/Private installs enable 'auth.signed_requests.enabled' to turn on signature verification. Recommended to test with staging key rotation script scripts/generate_signed_headers.sh. Monitor streaming-session auth failure rates and 5xxs during rollout.
security_impact: Introduces signed-request verification which reduces risk of replay attacks on private endpoints; includes guidance for key rotation and nonce handling. No credential format changes for hosted customers by default.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for header permutations, integration tests for streaming session nonces, end-to-end tests for OpenAI-compat header mapping. Addressed flaky streaming test by ensuring early nonce validation and session binding. Performance microbenchmarks included in CI artifacts.
changelog_entry: Auth: unify header semantics (scoped tokens, nonce), optional signed-request support for Private deployments, OpenAI-compat mapping for org headers.
notes_for_sdk_teams: Added helper functions in sdk/python/redwood/auth.py and sdk/typescript/src/auth.ts. SDK teams should add convenience wrappers for request signing if customers opt into signed-requests; examples provided in docs/openai-compat/auth.md.
user_visible_changes: No change for hosted customers by default. New capabilities for Dedicated/Private: optional signed-request verification, consistent scoped-token behavior, and clearer error responses for invalid nonce/signature.
risk_and_rollout_plan: Low-medium risk. Rollout plan: feature-flag disabled by default; enable in Dedicated staging clusters for 2 weeks; enable in Dedicated production; then offer to Private customers with migration checklist. Monitor auth failure rate and streaming errors. Have rollback plan to disable signed-request verification if unexpected failures observed.
